title: Learning Clusters: Hazira gas terminal release and fire, 2020
status: Learning purposes: not a statutory document; draft: the investigation status is in progress

incident.title: Hazira gas terminal condensate release and fire

data_quality.text: Draft learnings from an unreviewed analysis: the ProbeMatrix investigation status is in progress and no finding is marked as edited by a person. Validate before adoption.
The export mentions regulator involvement but its summary sheet says 'Reportable to Regulator: No'. Confirm the reporting status with the organisation; this pack does not decide it.

87 role strings could not be placed by the rules: 14 findings sit in F99 (no entity) and 87 in T9 (no tier). The Unresolved items table proposes a decision for each; the tables above it are the engine's counts before those proposals are applied.

bottom_line.text: Mechanical Maintenance (F02) holds the largest share of the learning: 194 findings, 91 of them top-rated. Its highest-rated findings are the lost seal specification and the missing return-to-service test on the condensate meter.

Operations & Control Room (F01) comes next with 170 findings, 72 top-rated. Its highest-rated findings sit after the release: isolation valves that could only be closed by hand at the valve, and gas detection with no automatic shutdown.
Engineering, Design, Documents & MOC (F07, 84 findings) owns the change and specification learning: a management-of-change procedure not used since 2018, and a gasket specification no one held.

HSE, Process Safety & Audit (F11, 80 findings) and Asset Integrity, Corrosion & Inspection (F05, 70 findings) carry the assurance and integrity learning: an emergency plan with no isolation criteria, and repeated seal failures treated as routine repairs.

Learning reaches every tier, but the board tier rests on one finding (T5), and 87 findings carry a role the rules could not place in a tier (T9). Entity placement is nearly complete: 14 findings sit in F99.

sections.heading: Learning clusters
sections.intro: A finding can touch several clusters, so the counts add up to more than the 436 findings. Three small clusters are not in the table: F16 Vendors, OEMs & Suppliers (7), F14 Corporate & Board (2) and F17 Contractors (2).

sections.heading: Tiers that must learn
sections.intro: A finding can name roles at several tiers. T9 counts findings with at least one role the rules could not place in a tier.

sections.heading: Relation mix
sections.intro: Almost every finding has an actor. One example role string per relation, from the export: actor, Maintenance team - gasket replacement crew; owner, Electrical Maintenance Team (FLP lamp owners); approver, Maintenance supervisor - approval authority; absent, Reliability Engineering (absent); learner, Maintenance Fitters (learners); norm-setter, Maintenance Supervisor (role model); challenger, Engineering authority (the role expected to challenge the deviation).

items.text: Owns the release source: the meter seal and the work on it. The highest-rated findings say the original gasket specification was lost and never re-established, so locally bought O-rings with no specification or quality check became the regular substitute [FND-A0017E28; EVD-8645], and that no procedure required a hydrostatic test before the meter went back into service [FND-50C7319E; EVD-2894].

Owns the response once the release began. The highest-rated findings say the emergency isolation valves were local-manual only, with no remote operation from the control room [FND-044D1DEC; EVD-3932], and that the fire and gas detection system had no automatic shutdown or suppression interlock [FND-6155A1C2; EVD-3452]. Its lower-tier findings cover accepting the meter back into service without a test.

Owns the design and change record. The highest-rated findings say the management-of-change procedure published in August 2016 had not been used since 2018, so the seal substitution was never reviewed [FND-F7FE8463; EVD-2986], and that the metering drawing was a vendor replacement, never approved, that did not match the field [FND-9D19BE37; EVD-0933].

Owns the plans and the assurance around them. The highest-rated findings say the on-site disaster management plan gave no isolation or stoppage criteria for a major hydrocarbon leak [FND-446A7956; EVD-4052], and a breakdown-led electrical maintenance culture left a damaged flame-proof lamp in service [FND-5E08D0F8; EVD-6916]. Its audit findings show generic checklists that could not find plant-specific defects [FND-C0466EB3; EVD-9692].

Owns the evidence that the equipment was deteriorating. The highest-rated findings say the meter kept failing at the seal and was left to routine resealing, with no root-cause or replacement programme [FND-1A251687; EVD-1494], and that pipe-wall loss found in 2017 had no corrective plan three years later [FND-C6992EAF; EVD-5527].

items.text: The workspace was classified with taxonomy 2.0 and the india-process-site overlay. The overlay adds the role words of an Indian public-sector process site: the site security force posts (constable, sub-inspector) go to Security & Surveillance (F10), the emergency plans (DMP, ERDMP) and the site and chief incident controllers go to Emergency Planning & Command (F09b), and GM, CGM and resident engineer ranks are read as plant leadership (T4). These are the roles of the night-shift command chain in the witness statements and the plant organogram [FND-4245FBF2; FND-82761CC5; EVD-3932].

limits: The proposed role decisions are not applied in this sample, so that its tables match a fresh setup of the export; an organisation running the coach applies them and re-runs classify.
No statutory posts were found in the role strings, so the Statutory posts section is left out.
Counts are finding instances, not learnings: one condition is often described by many findings.
